scope: Design decision; not implementation or platform acceptance evidence
fault_model: paused adopted Checker guardian that later resumes

mechanism.scheduler: Mise remains the sole DAG scheduler.
mechanism.cancellation: Only the root native guardian retains the broadcast writer. All participating guardians observe EOF independently. Nested normal completion does not cancel the invocation.
mechanism.completion: Each native guardian retains its parent completion writer until its direct child is reaped and its local cohort drains. EOF alone means descriptor closure, not universal reaping.
mechanism.lease: The same FD9 open-file description remains held throughout cleanup. Java receives neither lease nor lifecycle descriptors or locators.
mechanism.controllers: Substantive leaf controllers use native ownership. Clean standalone commands explicitly propagate verified context. Darwin nextest must survive to signal and reap its separate test/setup groups.
mechanism.linux: Retain the stronger existing subreaper cleanup, including escaped descendants carrying lifecycle descriptors. Kill/reap owned descendants before waiting on a barrier they could otherwise retain indefinitely.
mechanism.darwin: Cooperative cancellation and hierarchical acknowledgements require actual non-root Darwin verification. Direct mise exit and elapsed grace cannot certify completion.

boundaries: Existing Checker Darwin descendant prevention remains intact.
Arbitrary guardian SIGKILL is outside this decision’s ordinary fault model.
A controller crashing before forwarding to separate groups remains an explicitly uncovered fault unless additional custody is implemented.
evidence_sources: Read-only lifecycle_barrier_design scout reports in this session.
Existing process-supervision-design.json and retained pinned mise/nextest primary-source references.
acceptance: Open. Linux evidence alone cannot establish Darwin cleanup.
